_comment: Provenance for the VENDORED copy of the canonical sensitive-path fixture.
test/sensitive-paths-canon.test.ts recomputes the sha256 of the vendored
file and fails if it differs, so the fixture cannot be edited in this repo
without re-vendoring from the source below — a one-sided change cannot pass
CI silently. Same mechanism the hooks use for host-classification.json
(PKA-114); PKA-132 is the case where a canonical fixture was vendored stale
and nothing detected it.
To change the contract: change it in vinctor-conformance, then re-vendor
here AND in every sibling adapter, updating source + sha256 in each.
`source` MUST name a commit REACHABLE FROM vinctor-conformance main, and
the reachability MUST be checked before the sha is written down:
git -C <conformance> fetch --prune
git -C <conformance> merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main
Recompute the sha256 from that commit as well, rather than copying a value
out of a review comment. The point of this file is that nobody records a
pin they did not check.
That rule is not hypothetical. This pin was first written against the head
of the canon PR branch (pkachuc/vinctor-conformance#8) while it was still
open. The PR squash-merged as the commit below and the branch was deleted,
which left the earlier sha unreachable from every remote ref — the PKA-132
failure mode exactly: the bytes were still right, but nobody could re-derive
where they were supposed to have come from. A branch pin always dies this
way, so only a commit on main is a pin.
The vectors are DECOY strings to classify. Nothing here is a real path to
open: the conforming test never touches the filesystem.
